question: Should padding-only static evidence for GitHub-backed skills remain reviewer-only ClawScan input, or may it also set public suspicious visibility for otherwise installable skills?
rationale: The diff changes the boundary between deterministic static findings, final ClawScan verdicts, and public catalog visibility; that is a security/product policy choice that automation should not make implicitly.

options.title: Keep Evidence Reviewer-Only
options.body: Route padding findings through the current durable ClawScan flow and retain evidence without setting public suspicious state for padding-only results.

options.title: Approve Public Suspicious Visibility
options.body: Allow padding-only evidence to hide otherwise clean GitHub-backed skills, with explicit spec coverage, tests, and runtime proof of the user-facing impact.

options.title: Pause Security Direction
options.body: Keep the PR draft or close it until maintainers sponsor the scan-boundary and visibility policy.

recommendation.title: Keep Evidence Reviewer-Only
recommendation.body: Route padding findings through the current durable ClawScan flow and retain evidence without setting public suspicious state for padding-only results.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen owns the freshest current-main history for the GitHub-backed ClawScan boundary and is requested for review on the live PR.
